> The same simplification as example 002, written with `default ->` instead of `==`. It really is equivalent, so the verifier proves it and the build passes.

## The change

Collapse the four 'no refund outstanding' cases into a `default` branch.

**Before** ([`OrderLifecycle.java`](../../apps/boxoffice/ticketing-domain/src/main/java/net/terminalvalue/boxoffice/ticketing/domain/OrderLifecycle.java), line 46):

```java
    case PENDING_PAYMENT -> transition(DECLINED, RELEASE_SEATS);
    case CONFIRMED, DECLINED, REFUND_PENDING, REFUNDED -> unchanged("payment outcome already recorded");
};
case PaymentRefunded _ -> switch (current) {
    case REFUND_PENDING -> transition(REFUNDED);
    case PENDING_PAYMENT, CONFIRMED, DECLINED, REFUNDED -> unchanged("no refund outstanding");
};
case CancellationRequested _ -> switch (current) {
    case CONFIRMED -> transition(REFUND_PENDING, RELEASE_SEATS, REQUEST_REFUND);
    case REFUND_PENDING, REFUNDED -> unchanged("already cancelled");
    case PENDING_PAYMENT -> new Decision.Rejected("payment is in progress; try again shortly");
```

**After:**

```java
    case PENDING_PAYMENT -> transition(DECLINED, RELEASE_SEATS);
    case CONFIRMED, DECLINED, REFUND_PENDING, REFUNDED -> unchanged("payment outcome already recorded");
};
case PaymentRefunded _ -> switch (current) {
    case REFUND_PENDING -> transition(REFUNDED);
    default -> unchanged("no refund outstanding");
};
case CancellationRequested _ -> switch (current) {
    case CONFIRMED -> transition(REFUND_PENDING, RELEASE_SEATS, REQUEST_REFUND);
    case REFUND_PENDING, REFUNDED -> unchanged("already cancelled");
    case PENDING_PAYMENT -> new Decision.Rejected("payment is in progress; try again shortly");
```

## What the verifier found

All 36 possible inputs give the same outcome as the contract.

The contract file is unchanged, so the pull request contains code changes only.

## Would the existing tests have caught it?

Every existing unit test passes, as it should (`:ticketing-domain:test`, run against the patched code).

## Why it matters

None. This example shows the other half of the bargain: a check that also flagged safe refactors would be switched off within a week.

## Why the verdict is right

All 36 outcomes are identical, including decide(null, PaymentRefunded[]), because a switch over a null enum throws before any branch is chosen. The contract file is unchanged, so the pull request contains code changes only, and reviewers can tell from that alone that behaviour is preserved.

## What to do

Merge.
